title: PHYSICAL HEALTH EDUCATION (PE)-1
text:
THE KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATIONS COUNCIL
 SCHOOL BASED ASSESSMENT
 Physical and Health Education
 Grade 6 – 2022(Regular)
SECTION A (Written task on PHE skills and concepts 10 marks)
Instructions to the teacher
 1. This assessment is to be undertaken by all learners in Grade 6.
 2. This Section (Section A) consist of a written assessment task that assesses the learner’s
 acquisition of concepts in Physical and Health Education.
 3. The section has a total of 10 marks.
 4. Learners should respond to all the questions within the time allocated as shown in the
 question paper.
 5. Each learner is required to attempt all the items.
 6. Learners with disabilities should be assessed using the adapted assessment tools
 provided. Teachers may modify the adaptations suggested based on individual
 learner’s needs but should not compromise the outcome being assessed.
 7. Use the scoring guides provided to score each learner’s work and rate the performance
 accordingly.
 8. Use the appropriate mode of communication when instructing learners.
 9. Ensure that the assessment is done within the prescribed period.
 10. Share and discuss the assessment instructions with the learners so that they will know
 what is expected of them.
 11. Learners should be supervised when undertaking the written task to ensure validity of
 scores.
 12. Use the School Summary Assessment Score Sheet provided to capture the learners’
 performance levels for uploading.
 13. Maintain evidence of each learner’s performance for reference and quality assurance.

 Grade 6 – 2022 Scoring Guide
 (Regular)
Key for rating the learner’s performance
 i. Performance Level 4 (PL 4) (Exceeding Expectation) indicates that the learner has
 not only perfected /mastered the required skill but also exhibits exemplary skills that
 are above those required of his/her grade/age.
 ii. Performance Level 3 (PL 3) (Meeting Expectation) indicates that the learner has
 acquired the required skill.
iii. Performance Level 2 (PL 2) (Approaching Expectation) indicates that the learner
 has acquired some skills but has not fully mastered them.
 iv. Performance Level 2 PL 1 (Below Expectation) indicates that the learner is yet to
 develop the specified skills.
 SECTION A: TASK 1 -Written task on PHE skills and Concepts
 (The learner writes the responses in the space provided)
 1. Drop finish in athletics (1 mark)
 2. Scissor Kick (1 marks)
 3. Upright bars (1 mark)
 4. Take a crouch position in their respective lanes
 behind the starting line (1 mark)
 5. Swing kick (1 mark)
 6. Dribble (1 mark)
 7. Block the ball (1 mark)
 8. Shot put Landing Sector (1 mark)
 9. To completely stop the ball movement (1 Marks)
 10. Starting the game (1 Marks)
Rating of the Learner’s Performance
Task 1
 1. Use the scoring guide provided for questions 1 to 10 to score each learner's work.
 2. Rate the learner’s performance in task 1 under four performance levels as follows:
 i. Performance Level 4 (PL 4) (Exceeding Expectations) where the learner
 responds correctly to all the 10 questions.
 ii. Performance Level 3 (PL 3) (Meeting Expectations) where the learner
 responds correctly to 7, 8, or 9 Questions.
 iii. Performance Level 2 (PL 2) (Approaching Expectation) where the learner
 responds correctly to 4, 5, or 6 Questions.
 iv. Performance Level 1 (PL 1) (Below Expectation) where the learner responds
 correctly to 3, 2, or 1 Questions, OR does not respond correctly to any of the
 questions.
